curriculum.lesson_evidence: Australia’s location in the world can be described using hemispheres, neighbouring oceans and distance from other continents. Globes and world maps support accurate relative location.
curriculum.scope_limit: Proposed Stage 2 NESA HSIE alignment using catalogue outcome codes (HS2-*); content-point mapping and local First Nations protocols remain pending human review.

lesson.child_mission: Australia’s location in the world can be described using hemispheres, neighbouring oceans and distance from other continents. Globes and world maps support accurate relative location.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same HSIE idea to a new place or source, then compare two pieces of evidence for strength.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Name Australia’s hemisphere and two oceans that border or lie near Australia.

FEEDBACK
Southern Hemisphere; Indian Ocean and Pacific Ocean (accept Southern Ocean where taught).

WATCH FOR
Placing Australia in the middle of every mental map without oceans/continents confuses relative location.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Label a world map: Australia, six continents, three oceans, equator, Northern/Southern Hemisphere. Write two relative-location sentences.

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Australia’s location in the world can be described using hemispheres, neighbouring oceans and distance from other continents. Globes and world maps support accurate relative location.
materials: Optional: local map, photo or interview notes
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Label a world map: Australia, six continents, three oceans, equator, Northern/Southern Hemisphere. Write two relative-location sentences. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: Southern Hemisphere; Indian Ocean and Pacific Ocean (accept Southern Ocean where taught). Reasoning: I used world by attending to location rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Placing Australia in the middle of every mental map without oceans/continents confuses relative location. Correction: Southern Hemisphere; Indian Ocean and Pacific Ocean (accept Southern Ocean where taught). Why: the correction restores accurate use of world.

Parent: Likely misconception: Placing Australia in the middle of every mental map without oceans/continents confuses relative location. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating world on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with world, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Require independently produced work with a specific supporting detail. / Require misconception + correction + purpose-linked reason..
